description: Weighted fishing nets, including early forms comparable to seine or purse-style nets, were widely used by ancient cultures to harvest fish from rivers, lakes, and coastal waters. Made from flax, hemp, reeds, or other fibers, these nets were fitted with stone, ceramic, or lead weights along their lower edge so they would sink and encircle or trap schools of fish, while floats helped keep the upper edge near the surface. Such nets allowed communities around the Mediterranean, Near East, Europe, India, and East Asia to catch fish efficiently in large quantities, supporting both everyday subsistence and commercial food production.
